turns.text:
Community Literacy Collaborative has worked to strengthen family literacy in Riverview School District since 2016. Our mission is to build the reading skills, confidence, and routines that families need to support their children's academic success. Over the past decade we have served more than 500 families through peer-led reading groups, parent coaching, and school partnerships, giving us direct experience designing and delivering the type of programming proposed here. Our 2021–2023 Parents Read! pilot served 84 families, and 68% of participating K–3 children advanced at least one reading level within one year, while 74% of parents reported increased confidence supporting reading at home. That pilot shaped the Family Literacy Circles model and confirmed that peer-supported, coach-driven programming can produce measurable gains in both parent confidence and child outcomes.

Our team brings the qualifications this project requires. The Program Manager has experience overseeing multi-site family programs, managing partner agreements, and producing funder reports. The Evaluation Coordinator holds experience in program evaluation, data management, and FERPA-compliant data-sharing agreements, and will own the quarterly reporting process. Two part-time Circle Facilitators bring backgrounds in early childhood education and group facilitation, and two part-time Family Coaches have experience working directly with families facing barriers to school engagement. A contracted Data Analyst will clean, match, and analyze district assessment and attendance data, ensuring the rigor of pre/post and comparison analyses without requiring a permanent position. The organization is governed by a board of directors that reviews program and financial performance quarterly. Our fiscal systems include monthly financial reports, annual independent audits with no material findings over the past three years, payroll management, and structured grant reporting. In that period we have managed $1.2M in public and foundation grants with monthly budget-to-actual tracking. Two committed partners support delivery through signed MOUs. Riverview East Elementary School provides meeting space, student referrals, and attendance data under a data-sharing agreement. Westside Community Library provides circle hosting and childcare space in kind. Riverview Adult Learning Center refers parents seeking adult literacy or English-language support. These partnerships extend our reach without duplicating services. Quality assurance is built into the program through quarterly indicator reviews, second-person data entry checks, 10% random audits of survey and log data, and duplicate ID checks before each data merge. If an outcome trails its target for two consecutive quarters, the Program Manager convenes the team to adjust circle structure, coaching dosage, or recruitment, and documents the change in the next report. After the grant period, Community Literacy Collaborative will sustain the program through a diversified funding strategy that includes local foundation grants, public funding applications, and continued partner in-kind contributions. The peer parent leader pipeline, in which graduates of each cohort are trained to co-facilitate future circles, reduces long-term staffing costs and builds community ownership of the program.
